Tradeoff: `@package.json` auto-syncs but pulls in deps/config noise and loses your inline annotations (e.g. "Start API + landing in background", "no build artifact"). The current list is curated — it tells me *which* commands matter and *why*, which package.json can't.

_**User (2026-04-11 22:02:37Z)**_

what other approaches might we take to keep them automatically in sync? (can package.json import these from a standalone scripts json file?)

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-6 2026-04-11 22:02:50Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-6 2026-04-11 22:02:57Z)**_

No, package.json can't natively import scripts from another file — npm reads only the `scripts` field in that exact file. Options:

1. **Generator script** — keep a `scripts.json` (or YAML) with `{command, description}` pairs as the source of truth; a small node script writes both `package.json` scripts and a marker-delimited block in CLAUDE.md (`<!-- scripts:start --> ... <!-- scripts:end -->`). Run it in a `prepare` hook or pre-commit.

2. **Drift check instead of sync** — a test/CI step that parses package.json and asserts every script appears in CLAUDE.md (or vice versa). Cheaper than generation, catches staleness without owning the content.

3. **`better-scripts` / `ntl` / `scripty`** — tools that let you attach descriptions to npm scripts, but they don't feed CLAUDE.md.

For this repo I'd lean toward **#2**: a 20-line vitest that diffs the two. Generation is more machinery than a single-file Worker needs, and the drift check still lets you curate the CLAUDE.md wording.

1	---
2	type: note
3	status: inbox

5	---
6	
7	# Preserve original APOD filename on download
8	
9	When a user downloads an image from `api.nasapicture.com` (or `get.`), the browser saves it as `api.nasapicture.jpg`, derived from the hostname because the URL path has no meaningful filename. We should set `Content-Disposition` so downloads use the original NASA asset name (e.g. `NGC1234_hubble1200.jpg`), preserving provenance and making the filename searchable against apod.nasa.gov.
10	
11	## Problem
12	
13	All image endpoints currently return only `Content-Type`, so browsers fall back to `<hostname>.<ext>` when the user hits "Save image as...". Every image from the proxy ends up named the same thing, which is unhelpful for anyone collecting wallpapers or citing sources.
14	
15	## Proposed fix
16	
17	Add a `Content-Disposition: inline; filename="<original>"` header to image responses. Using `inline` (not `attachment`) keeps the image displayed in-browser when hit directly, and only influences the filename on save.
18	
19	The original filename is always the last path segment of the NASA URL:
20	
21	```
22	https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/image/2604/NGC1234_hubble1200.jpg
23	                                      └───────── filename ──┘
24	```
25	
26	`resolved.imageHdUrl` / `resolved.imageUrl` in `src/index.ts` already hold this URL by the time we build the response, so extraction is a one-liner.
27	
28	## Affected endpoints
29	
30	From `src/index.ts:608-685`:
31	
32	- `/` and `/image.jpg` — serve `imageHdUrl`, extension matches source
33	- `/sd` and `/image-sd.jpg` — serve `imageUrl` (standard res), extension matches source
34	- `/optimized` and `/image-optimized.jpg` — **extension needs rewriting**: the response may be WebP/AVIF depending on `Accept`, so we should swap the original extension to match the actual `Content-Type` the transform returned
35	- `/thumb` and `/thumb.jpg` — same caveat as optimized (always WebP). Lower priority since thumbnails aren't meant for downloading, but consistency is cheap.
36	- `/info` and `/about` — skip, not image responses
37	
38	## Implementation sketch
39	
40	1. Add a helper:
41	   ```ts
42	   function filenameFromUrl(url: string, overrideExt?: string): string {
43	     const pathname = new URL(url).pathname;
44	     const last = pathname.split("/").pop() || "apod.jpg";
45	     // Strip anything unsafe for a header value, keep it ASCII.
46	     const safe = last.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, "_");
47	     if (!overrideExt) return safe;
48	     return safe.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, `.${overrideExt}`);
49	   }
50	   ```
51	2. In each image branch, compute the filename and pass it into `baseHeaders` (or set directly on the response):
52	   ```ts
53	   "Content-Disposition": `inline; filename="${filename}"`,
54	   ```
55	3. For `/optimized` and `/thumb`, derive `overrideExt` from the actual response `Content-Type` (`image/webp` → `webp`, `image/avif` → `avif`, else `jpg`).
56	
57	## Safety notes
58	
59	- NASA image URLs are trusted (validated by `validateImageUrl`), but a filename is still header input. Restrict to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` so a malformed URL can't inject a CR/LF or a stray `"`.
60	- Video thumbnails come from YouTube/Vimeo (`maxresdefault.jpg`, etc.) and won't have meaningful names. That's fine — any original filename is better than `api.nasapicture.jpg`.
61	- `Content-Disposition` with `inline` does NOT force a download; it only affects the suggested filename if the user chooses to save. Existing `<img src>` consumers are unaffected.
62	
63	## Out of scope
64	
65	- RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''...` encoding for non-ASCII names. NASA filenames are ASCII in practice; revisit only if that changes.
66	- Changing the route URLs themselves (e.g. `/image/NGC1234.jpg`). That would affect caching and is a bigger design call.
67	
68	## Acceptance
69	
70	- `curl -I https://api.nasapicture.com/ | grep -i content-disposition` returns the original NASA filename.
71	- Saving the image in a browser uses that filename, not `api.nasapicture.jpg`.
72	- `/optimized` download filenames carry `.webp` / `.avif` when the response is transformed.
73	- Existing image consumers (landing page, `<img>` embeds) still work identically.
74
```

---
type: note
status: inbox
created: 2026-04-11

# Drift check between CLAUDE.md commands and package.json scripts

The Commands section in `CLAUDE.md` hand-lists every npm script with a short description. It's useful curation (I can tell Claude *why* a command matters), but it silently drifts as scripts are added, renamed, or removed. Package.json can't natively import scripts from another file, so keeping them in sync needs tooling.

## Options considered

1. **`@package.json` reference in CLAUDE.md** — auto-syncs but pulls in deps/config noise and drops the inline annotations.
2. **Generator script** — maintain a `scripts.json` source of truth; a node script writes both `package.json` scripts and a marker-delimited block in CLAUDE.md on `prepare` or pre-commit. Most machinery, strongest guarantee.
3. **Drift check test** (this note) — a small vitest that parses `package.json` and asserts every script is mentioned in `CLAUDE.md` (or vice versa). Doesn't own the content, just catches staleness.

## Proposed approach

A single vitest under `test/` that:

- Reads `package.json` and extracts `scripts` keys.
- Reads `CLAUDE.md` and finds the fenced `bash` block under `## Commands`.
- Parses script names out of that block (`npm run <name>` or `npm <name>`).
- Fails if either side has entries missing from the other.

Optionally allow a small allowlist constant in the test for scripts we intentionally omit from CLAUDE.md (internal-only helpers), so the test stays a curation aid rather than a forcing function.

## Why this over generation

- Single-file Worker repo, low churn; generation is more machinery than the problem warrants.
- Curated wording in CLAUDE.md is the whole value — a generator would have to learn descriptions anyway.
- A failing test is self-explanatory and runs in CI alongside everything else.

## Acceptance

- `npm test` fails if a script is added to `package.json` without being documented in `CLAUDE.md` (or removed without being cleaned up).
- Allowlist mechanism exists for intentionally-undocumented scripts, with a comment explaining why each is excluded.
- Test runs in under a second and has no external dependencies.
